title: Build a minimal family document, load it into the project, and place an instance
task: Create a custom component the project lacks: make a family document from a family template (Generic Model.rft), draw an extrusion in it, load it into the project with Document.LoadFamily, activate a FamilySymbol and place a FamilyInstance with NewFamilyInstance.

pitfalls.symptom: script-target-must-not-be-modifiable: 'The document must not be modifiable before calling LoadFamily' when LoadFamily is called inside Connector.WithTransaction(doc, ...).
pitfalls.cause: LoadFamily commits its own transaction on the target project and refuses a target with a transaction open; the block holds one.
pitfalls.fix: Call LoadFamily at top level, between blocks (step 4); place the instance in a block afterwards.

pitfalls.symptom: NewFamilyInstance throws for a freshly loaded family's symbol.
pitfalls.cause: A FamilySymbol that has never been placed is inactive.
pitfalls.fix: Check symbol.IsActive and call symbol.Activate() first (step 5).

pitfalls.cause: A family with the same name is already loaded in the project.
pitfalls.fix: Use LoadFamily(doc, IFamilyLoadOptions) to overwrite, or find the existing Family by Name with a FilteredElementCollector and place from it.

pitfalls.symptom: The family document is still open after the run.
pitfalls.cause: Document.Close is a lifecycle action, gated behind confirm_lifecycle_actions, so the script leaves it open.
pitfalls.fix: Close it in a later call with confirm_lifecycle_actions: true, or leave it; a throw in this run rolls the created document back automatically.
